assumptions_challenged: The program has generated and characterized a Master Cell Bank (MCB) or Working Cell Bank (WCB).
Orthogonal QC assays (including validated intact‑EV assays with defined LLOQ, specificity, and precision) have been developed and validated for the program material.
There exist ≥3 GMP‑like batch records demonstrating reproducible release results and within‑/between‑batch comparability for the program material.
Stability studies and a stability‑indicating potency assay have been completed and correlated to an in vivo PD endpoint for the program material.

Formulation and device compatibility data demonstrate recovery of intact EV in relevant matrices and controlled intranasal delivery in large animals with orthogonal controls attributing signal to intact EVs rather than free cargo or non‑vesicular particles.
Rodent intranasal biodistribution data alone are sufficient to predict reproducible intact‑EV CNS exposure in larger species without matched intact‑EV analytics and bridging controls.
falsification_conditions: Program submits MCB/WCB generation and characterization reports (identity, mycoplasma/adventitious agent testing, cell characterization) showing acceptable source‑cell controls.

Program submits validated orthogonal QC panel method validation reports including intact‑EV assay validation with documented LLOQ, specificity, accuracy/precision (intra/inter‑assay), linearity, and robustness tied to release specifications.
Program provides ≥3 GMP‑like batch production reports with release test results and statistical comparability demonstrating acceptable within‑ and between‑batch variability for defined CQAs.
Program provides stability study reports demonstrating stability‑indicating behavior and a potency assay whose results correlate with an in vivo PD endpoint (data and statistical correlation).

Program provides formulation/device compatibility recovery data (ex vivo and in vivo) showing preserved intact‑EV markers and functional potency post‑processing, with appropriate orthogonal controls separating intact EV signal from free cargo/non‑vesicular particles.

Program provides controlled large‑animal intranasal biodistribution bridging studies using validated intact‑EV assays and orthogonal controls that attribute observed CNS or tissue signals to intact EVs and demonstrate reproducibility across lots/species.
strongest_objection: The record contains only MISEV2023 consensus guidance and no program-specific CMC/analytics/batch/stability or controlled biodistribution data; therefore the program cannot justify advancing an intranasal EV formulation or starting cross‑species PK/PD bridging until the Stage‑1 CMC/analytics/formulation compatibility package is produced and reviewed.
